blurb: Compact, muscular English terrier from Staffordshire with a short, close coat
description: The Staffordshire Bull Terrier is a small to medium terrier from England with a short, close coat and broad head, described as bold and family-friendly.
answer: The Staffordshire Bull Terrier, or Staffy, is a small to medium terrier that originated in Staffordshire and the northern parts of Birmingham in England. It descends from nineteenth-century bull and terrier crosses, is muscular and broad-headed with a short coat, and is described by the Kennel Club as bold, fearless and well suited to families.

body: After bull- and bear-baiting were outlawed in 1835, breeders crossed bulldogs with terriers, producing the bull and terrier type that also gave rise to the Bull Terrier; the type was used for dog fighting, which delayed official recognition. Led by Joseph Dunn, fanciers persuaded the Kennel Club to recognise the breed in 1935, and a breed club and standard followed that year in Cradley Heath. The FCI recognised it in 1954 and the American Kennel Club in 1974.

The Stafford is about as long from withers to tail as it is tall, typically standing 36–41 cm, with dogs weighing about 13–17 kg and bitches roughly 2 kg less. It has a broad head, ears that fold at the tip, strong shoulders and a wide chest. The coat is short, stiff and close, in white, black, blue, fawn or red, with or without white, or any brindle.

The Kennel Club describes the breed as bold, fearless and totally reliable, and the standard notes a particular affinity with children; the AKC calls it a mild, playful companion. It is also said not to back away when challenged by another dog.
The breed is described as agile and quite active. Sources give little further detail on exercise or grooming, though the short, close coat is generally considered simple to maintain.

Conditions reported in the breed include juvenile-onset demodicosis, hereditary cataracts and neurological disorders such as cerebellar abiotrophy, Chiari-like malformation, myotonia congenita and L-2-hydroxyglutaric aciduria. A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12 years.

faq.q: How big does a Staffordshire Bull Terrier get?
faq.a: Staffords usually stand 36–41 cm at the withers and weigh about 11–17 kg, with bitches a little lighter than dogs.

faq.q: Are Staffordshire Bull Terriers good with children?
faq.a: The Kennel Club recommends the breed for families, and its standard notes a particular affinity with children.

faq.q: Is a Staffordshire Bull Terrier a pit bull?
faq.a: No. It is a separate recognised breed, though it shares bull and terrier ancestry with pit bull types and is often confused with them.

faq.q: How long do Staffordshire Bull Terriers live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12 years, and a 2022 UK study found 11.33 years.
